rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Diff-risk line: chunk 4, line 27: "For this first session, fifteen to thirty minutes is enough." "this first session" resolves to "Session one" named in chunk 2, line 13 ("Session one goes now, un-packaged...") under the sequential deck read carve-out (term introduced on an earlier slide, reused) — only one candidate session exists by this point in the deck, so it is not vague-with-history. Also checked chunk 4 line 25 "stop it": "it" resolves in-sentence to "Claude" named earlier in the same clause. No unresolved referent found.

Closest candidate: chunk 1, line 9: "You're new to this country: the stretch where the agent runs alone and you don't watch each step." The "country" metaphor is module-arc vocabulary named in the enclosing module's own opener (run-the-first-experiment.md maintainer note: "the far half names the country") and reused here by NAME, not by page position, so it clears §2's ban on locating another file positionally (the module-include-order carve-out under rule 1 applies). grep confirms zero phrases matching cross-file positional patterns ("opening lecture said", "earlier module", "prior module", "last lecture") anywhere in body lines 1-27: `sed -n '1,27p' ... | grep -niE "opening lecture|earlier module|prior module|the module before|last lecture"` -> no output.

Every chunk carries multiple self-carrying sentences/bullets, not a lone wait-state line: chunk 1 (lines 3-9) develops the experiment framing and the tourist/practitioner claim across 3 paragraphs; chunk 2 (11-15) states the full two-session contrast in 3 bullets; chunk 3 (17-21) defines gap-analysis, its question, and the find-vs-judge split; chunk 4 (23-27) covers cancel-is-legitimate, trace sufficiency, and session length in 3 bullets. No chunk is a single context-dependent fragment.

Line closest to drifting from its header: chunk 4 header "Cancel is legitimate; traces are data" vs line 27 "Session length follows the task and how well your checks guide it." — this bullet doesn't literally say "cancel" but stays inside the header's second clause (traces ARE data, so how much trace/session you need is the header's own topic); it continues directly from line 26's "beats hours of trace you can't read," the same claim the header states. This placement is an unchanged carryover from the maintainer's 2026-07-02 slides-only pass ("its unique operational line... CONVERTED into the last slide's third bullet"), reviewed and passed at two prior pins; the run-to-session diff does not touch structure.

Checked every sub-item across all 4 body chunks. "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction: absent (grep for repeated "Not " clause opens found none). Anaphora/epistrophe triples: closest candidate is the diff itself — "session" appears 3x across chunk 4 lines 26-27 ("A short session", "this first session", "Session length") — but this does NOT match the rule's specific pattern, which requires a structural triple of PARALLEL sentence-initial or sentence-final repeats (the compendium's own example: "Every session inherited... Every session got better. Every session reached..."). Here the 3 uses sit in different grammatical positions (object of preposition, adverbial-clause noun, subject) across only 2 sentences, not a 3-clause parallel structure, so rule 7's anaphora/epistrophe sub-item does not fire. (Flagged separately in `notes` as a check_writing.md register/repetition question, out of this class's lane.) Self-grading superlatives: absent. Number + own retraction: "twenty minutes" (line 25) and "fifteen to thirty minutes" (line 27) are both stated once, not retracted afterward — not this pattern. Abstraction-noun stacks: absent ("thin spots", "gaps" are concrete, not abstraction-stacked). Verb triplets with an empty leg: absent.
